transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things that I normally handle fine. Like, you know, returning calls at work or turning in a registration form, or even just stopping for an errand on the way home. Which is funny because there's this little grocery store right on my route home, the one with the really good local honey? I love their honey. I usually get the clover one, but last week they had this wildflower batch that was just amazing. I meant to pick up more, but I drove right past it three days in a row. My husband was like, "Didn't you say you were getting honey?" and I just completely blanked. But yeah, I'm just dropping the ball on these little everyday tasks and it's getting frustrating.
When you were a child, did you also have trouble staying organized or remembering everyday tasks?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Even back in elementary school... I was always that kid who forgot permission slips, or I'd somehow lose my finished homework right in my own backpack. I had this huge purple backpack, I think it was from L.L. Bean? You know how those things last forever? My mom actually still uses it to store her knitting supplies. She knits these amazing little baby blankets, she just made a really cute yellow one for my cousin's new baby. 

But yeah, my backpack was just a total black hole for papers. And school projects were the worst. I always needed my mom or my teacher to literally sit there and remind me, like, step by step to actually finish them. Otherwise I'd just get caught up in picking out the right markers for the cover page and completely forget to do the actual work.
Do these problems with forgetting and staying organized happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere. I mean, I’m still getting by, you know? But it is happening at work and at home. I've missed enough small work follow-ups and, like, my kids' school deadlines lately that I'm really starting to worry it's going to affect my reputation. Which is a big deal right now because I really want to move into this Office Manager role at my company. 

The current Office Manager, Linda, is actually retiring in the spring. She and her husband bought this massive RV and they're just going to drive around the country. I think they're starting in Arizona because she absolutely hates the cold. I don't blame her, honestly, the winters here are getting brutal. My own heater at home has been making this weird clanking noise for a week and I keep meaning to call the repair guy, but... well, there's another thing I forgot to do. 

But, um, anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the promotion. Yeah, I just worry that if I keep dropping the ball on these little things, the bosses are gonna notice and completely pass me over for Linda's job.
Do you still have these forgetting and organization problems during times when your mood is good and you’re not feeling especially anxious?

Um, yeah, I'd say so. It's not really about how I'm feeling, you know? Like, even on a really good day, when everything's fine and I'm not stressed at all, I'll still walk into the kitchen and completely forget why I went in there. Or I'll leave my coffee in the microwave for three hours. I actually got this new coffee blend recently, it's a hazelnut roast from that little cafe downtown? The one with the green awning? They roast their own beans right there in the back, and it smells amazing when you walk by. I usually just get regular drip coffee, but the barista talked me into trying it. He was super nice, actually, he said he's studying graphic design at the community college. I think his name was... Tyler? Or maybe Taylor? 

Anyway, it's a really good coffee, but it tastes terrible when you have to reheat it three times because you keep forgetting you made it. So yeah, it doesn't really matter if I'm happy or anxious or whatever, the forgetting just kind of happens no matter what.
Have these attention and organization problems caused significant problems in your work, home life, or relationships?

Um, no, I wouldn't say *significant* problems. Like, my husband gets a little annoyed sometimes when I forget to do things around the house, but it's not a huge deal. Like last week, I left the wet clothes in the washing machine for two days and they got that awful mildew smell. You know how hard it is to get that out of towels? I had to buy this special vinegar wash stuff online. The bottle took forever to ship, too, because I think it came all the way from Oregon. 

I've always wanted to visit Oregon, actually. My sister went to Portland a few years ago and said the food trucks there are just incredible. She had this gourmet grilled cheese with, like, fig jam and brie on sourdough. I actually tried to recreate it at home once, but I totally burned the bread because I walked away to answer a work email and completely forgot the pan was on the stove. The smoke alarm went off and everything. We had to open all the windows and order pizza instead. We usually get from Luigi's down the street, they have the absolute best garlic knots. They put this little side of marinara in the box that is just perfectly seasoned. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, relationships and work. Yeah, no, my husband just kind of sighed and ate the pizza. We don't really have big fights about my forgetfulness or anything. And at work, like I said, I'm still getting by without any real trouble. So no, nothing major.
Have these attention and organization problems ever caused you to lose a job, fail a class, or seriously damage an important relationship?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't lost any jobs or failed out of school or anything. Like I said before, I'm still getting by. I just... I've missed enough of those small work follow-ups and my kids' school deadlines that I'm starting to worry. It's just happening often enough that I'm scared it's going to affect my reputation, you know? And I really, really want that Office Manager role when Linda leaves. 

Linda's actually the one who hired me, years ago. She's been there forever. She has this huge collection of ceramic frogs on her desk. Like, dozens of them. People just started bringing them to her as gifts from their vacations, and now they take up half her workspace. There's this one from Mexico that's wearing a tiny sombrero, it's actually really cute. I went to Mexico once, for my honeymoon. We stayed in Cancun, but we took a day trip to see the Mayan ruins. It was so hot that day, I think I drank like six bottles of water. My husband got a terrible sunburn on the back of his neck because he refused to wear a hat. He's so stubborn about hats. He says they make his head itch. 

But, um... yeah, no lost jobs or ruined relationships. Just the worry about my reputation and the promotion.
